findings.issue: IAM user has no registered MFA device
findings.risk: An unprotected console password increases account takeover risk. MFA enrollment alone does not enforce MFA for access-key API requests.
findings.remediation: For human access, prefer federation/Identity Center with enforced MFA. If this IAM user remains, register MFA and enforce it through access policy; replace workload users with roles.

findings.risk: A global ACL grant may permit unintended bucket access. Public does not prove network reachability or object access.
findings.remediation: Review the grants, remove unintended global grantees, and enable IgnorePublicAcls and BlockPublicAcls at the appropriate scopes.

evidence.scope_note: Bucket/account configuration only; organisation controls and object ACLs are not evaluated.

findings.issue: S3 classifies the bucket policy as public
findings.risk: The bucket policy is classified as public by S3 and the observed controls do not establish that public access is restricted.
findings.remediation: Review bucket-policy principals and conditions; remove unintended public access and enable RestrictPublicBuckets and BlockPublicPolicy where appropriate.

limitations: This is a configuration review, not a penetration test or proof of internet reachability.
S3 coverage is bucket ACLs and S3 policy-public status, with observed bucket/account Block Public Access. Object ACLs, access points and organisation-level controls are excluded.

IAM policy checks inspect attached managed permission policies and user/role/group inline policies. They do not compute effective permissions, trust policies, SCPs, permission boundaries or session policies.
IAM MFA checks cover IAM users, not the root user, federated identities or Identity Center. Enrollment is distinct from enforcement.
Security-group checks cover universal IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs and unrestricted egress in explicitly selected regions; routes, NACLs, attachments and combinations of non-universal CIDRs are not evaluated.
